task: r01t_fromager_distinfo_ticket
prompt: 'This is the fromager repository (Python wheel builder). A virtualenv with the project

  and test dependencies is already set up at `.venv`; run tests with

  `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -o addopts="" tests/...`.


  Fix the issue below. Add a regression test and run the relevant test file.


  Issue #1146: get_metadata_for_wheel() may return wrong metadata


  `get_metadata_for_wheel` returns the first match for `name.endswith(".dist-info/METADATA")`.

  This is a bad assumption. A wheel can contain multiple `.dist-info` directories. It''s

  common to include dist-info directories of vendored packages.


  `get_metadata_for_wheel` should only look at `dist-info` directories in the root of the

  wheel. Or better: parse the URL, split the name, and use

  `{dist_name}-{dist_version}.dist-info/METADATA`.

  '

import dataclasses
import datetime
import logging
import posixpath
import typing
from io import BytesIO
from urllib.parse import unquote, urlparse
from zipfile import ZipFile

from packaging.metadata import Metadata
from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.utils import (
    BuildTag,
    InvalidWheelFilename,
    canonicalize_name,
    parse_wheel_filename,
)
from packaging.version import Version

from .request_session import session

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


@dataclasses.dataclass
class Cooldown:
    """Policy for rejecting recently-published package versions.

    bootstrap_time is fixed at construction so all resolutions in a single run
    share the same cutoff.
    """

    min_age: datetime.timedelta
    bootstrap_time: datetime.datetime = dataclasses.field(
        default_factory=lambda: datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC)
    )


@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True, order=True, slots=True, repr=False, kw_only=True)
class Candidate:
    name: str
    version: Version
    url: str
    is_sdist: bool | None = dataclasses.field(default=None)
    extras: tuple[str, ...] = dataclasses.field(default=(), compare=False)
    build_tag: BuildTag = dataclasses.field(default=(), compare=False)
    has_metadata: bool = dataclasses.field(default=False, compare=False)
    remote_tag: str | None = dataclasses.field(default=None, compare=False)
    remote_commit: str | None = dataclasses.field(default=None, compare=False)
    upload_time: datetime.datetime | None = dataclasses.field(
        default=None, compare=False
    )

    _metadata: Metadata | None = dataclasses.field(
        default=None, init=False, compare=False
    )
    _dependencies: list[Requirement] | None = dataclasses.field(
        default=None, init=False, compare=False
    )

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        # force normalized name
        object.__setattr__(self, "name", canonicalize_name(self.name))

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        if not self.extras:
            return f"<{self.name}=={self.version}>"
        return f"<{self.name}[{','.join(self.extras)}]=={self.version}>"

    @property
    def metadata_url(self) -> str | None:
        """PEP 658: metadata is available at {url}.metadata"""
        if self.has_metadata:
            return self.url + ".metadata"
        return None

    @property
    def metadata(self) -> Metadata:
        if self._metadata is None:
            if not self.has_metadata:
                raise ValueError(f"{self.url} does not have metadata")
            metadata = get_metadata_for_wheel(self.url, self.metadata_url)
            object.__setattr__(self, "_metadata", metadata)
        assert self._metadata
        return self._metadata

    def _get_dependencies(self) -> typing.Iterable[Requirement]:
        deps = self.metadata.requires_dist or []
        extras = self.extras if self.extras else [""]

        for r in deps:
            if r.marker is None:
                yield r
            else:
                for e in extras:
                    if r.marker.evaluate({"extra": e}):
                        yield r

    @property
    def dependencies(self) -> list[Requirement]:
        if self._dependencies is None:
            dependencies = list(self._get_dependencies())
            object.__setattr__(self, "_dependencies", dependencies)
        assert self._dependencies
        return self._dependencies

    @property
    def requires_python(self) -> str | None:
        spec = self.metadata.requires_python
        return str(spec) if spec is not None else None


def get_metadata_for_wheel(
    url: str, metadata_url: str | None = None, *, validate: bool = True
) -> Metadata:
    """Get metadata for a wheel, supporting PEP 658 metadata endpoints.

    Args:
        url: URL of the wheel file
        metadata_url: Optional URL of the metadata file (PEP 658)
        validate: Whether to validate metadata (default: True)

    Returns:
        Parsed metadata as a Metadata object
    """
    # Try PEP 658 metadata endpoint first if available
    if metadata_url:
        try:
            logger.debug(
                f"Attempting to fetch metadata from PEP 658 endpoint: {metadata_url}"
            )
            response = session.get(metadata_url)
            response.raise_for_status()

            # Parse metadata directly using packaging.metadata.Metadata
            # (avoiding circular import with dependencies module)
            metadata = Metadata.from_email(response.content, validate=validate)
            logger.debug(f"Successfully retrieved metadata via PEP 658 for {url}")
            return metadata

        except Exception as e:
            logger.debug(f"Failed to fetch PEP 658 metadata from {metadata_url}: {e}")
            logger.debug(
                "Falling back to downloading full wheel for metadata extraction"
            )

    # Fallback to existing method: download wheel and extract metadata
    logger.debug(f"Downloading full wheel to extract metadata: {url}")
    data = session.get(url).content
    metadata_path = _get_metadata_path_for_wheel_url(url)
    with ZipFile(BytesIO(data)) as z:
        try:
            metadata_content = z.read(metadata_path)
        except KeyError:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Could not find {metadata_path} in wheel: {url}"
            ) from None
    # Parse metadata directly using packaging.metadata.Metadata
    # (avoiding circular import with dependencies module)
    return Metadata.from_email(metadata_content, validate=validate)


def _get_metadata_path_for_wheel_url(url: str) -> str:
    """Get path of the wheel's own METADATA file from the wheel URL.

    Wheels may contain ``.dist-info`` directories of vendored packages, so
    the path is derived from the wheel filename instead of searching.
    """
    wheel_filename = posixpath.basename(unquote(urlparse(url).path))
    # parse_wheel_filename normalizes the dist name, however the dist-info
    # directory uses the verbatim distribution name from the wheel file.
    try:
        _, dist_version, _, _ = parse_wheel_filename(wheel_filename)
    except InvalidWheelFilename as err:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid wheel filename in URL: {url}") from err
    dist_name = wheel_filename.split("-", 1)[0]
    return f"{dist_name}-{dist_version}.dist-info/METADATA"

+    @patch("fromager.candidate.session")

+        """Test that METADATA of vendored packages in the wheel is ignored."""

"""Tests for PEP 658 metadata support."""

import io
import typing
import zipfile
from unittest.mock import Mock, patch

import pytest
from packaging.version import Version

from fromager.candidate import Candidate, get_metadata_for_wheel


class TestPEP658Support:
    """Test PEP 658 metadata support in fromager."""

    def test_candidate_with_metadata_url(self) -> None:
        """Test that Candidate can be created with a metadata URL."""
        candidate = Candidate(
            name="test-package",
            version=Version("1.0.0"),
            url="https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            has_metadata=True,
        )

        assert (
            candidate.metadata_url
            == "https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl.metadata"
        )

    def test_candidate_without_metadata_url(self) -> None:
        """Test that Candidate works without metadata URL (legacy behavior)."""
        candidate = Candidate(
            name="test-package",
            version=Version("1.0.0"),
            url="https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
        )

        assert candidate.metadata_url is None

    @patch("fromager.candidate.session")
    def test_get_metadata_with_pep658_success(self, mock_session: typing.Any) -> None:
        """Test successful metadata retrieval via PEP 658 endpoint."""
        # Mock the metadata response
        mock_response = Mock()
        mock_response.content = b"""Metadata-Version: 2.1
Name: test-package
Version: 1.0.0
Summary: A test package
Requires-Dist: requests >= 2.0.0
"""
        mock_response.raise_for_status.return_value = None
        mock_session.get.return_value = mock_response

        wheel_url = "https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl"
        metadata_url = (
            "https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl.metadata"
        )

        metadata = get_metadata_for_wheel(wheel_url, metadata_url)

        # Verify the metadata was parsed correctly
        assert metadata.name == "test-package"
        assert str(metadata.version) == "1.0.0"
        assert metadata.summary == "A test package"
        assert metadata.requires_dist is not None
        assert any(str(req) == "requests>=2.0.0" for req in metadata.requires_dist)

        # Verify only the metadata URL was called, not the wheel URL
        mock_session.get.assert_called_once_with(metadata_url)

    @patch("fromager.candidate.session")
    def test_get_metadata_pep658_fallback_behavior(
        self, mock_session: typing.Any
    ) -> None:
        """Test that PEP 658 is tried first, then falls back to wheel download."""
        # Mock that metadata URL fails, then wheel URL succeeds
        responses = []

        def side_effect(url: str) -> typing.Any:
            if url.endswith(".metadata"):
                # First call - metadata request fails
                mock_response = Mock()
                mock_response.raise_for_status.side_effect = Exception("404 Not Found")
                responses.append(("metadata", url))
                return mock_response
            else:
                # Second call - wheel request
                responses.append(("wheel", url))
                raise Exception("Wheel parsing intentionally mocked to fail")

        mock_session.get.side_effect = side_effect

        wheel_url = "https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl"
        metadata_url = (
            "https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl.metadata"
        )

        # This should raise an exception during wheel parsing, but we can verify the order
        try:
            get_metadata_for_wheel(wheel_url, metadata_url)
        except Exception:
            pass  # Expected to fail during wheel parsing mock

        # Verify that both URLs were called in the correct order
        assert len(responses) == 2
        assert responses[0] == ("metadata", metadata_url)
        assert responses[1] == ("wheel", wheel_url)
        assert mock_session.get.call_count == 2

    @patch("fromager.candidate.session")
    def test_get_metadata_without_pep658_behavior(
        self, mock_session: typing.Any
    ) -> None:
        """Test that without PEP 658 metadata URL, only wheel URL is called."""
        # Mock wheel request
        responses = []

        def side_effect(url: str) -> typing.Any:
            responses.append(("wheel", url))
            raise Exception("Wheel parsing intentionally mocked to fail")

        mock_session.get.side_effect = side_effect

        wheel_url = "https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl"

        # This should raise an exception during wheel parsing, but we can verify the behavior
        try:
            get_metadata_for_wheel(wheel_url, metadata_url=None)
        except Exception:
            pass  # Expected to fail during wheel parsing mock

        # Verify that only the wheel URL was called
        assert len(responses) == 1
        assert responses[0] == ("wheel", wheel_url)
        mock_session.get.assert_called_once_with(wheel_url)

    @patch("fromager.candidate.session")
    def test_get_metadata_ignores_vendored_dist_info(
        self, mock_session: typing.Any
    ) -> None:
        """Test that METADATA of vendored packages in the wheel is ignored."""
        buf = io.BytesIO()
        with zipfile.ZipFile(buf, "w") as zf:
            # vendored dist-info sorts and is written before the real one
            zf.writestr(
                "My_Pkg/_vendor/aaa-2.0.dist-info/METADATA",
                "Metadata-Version: 2.1\nName: aaa\nVersion: 2.0\n",
            )
            zf.writestr(
                "My_Pkg-1.0.0.dist-info/METADATA",
                "Metadata-Version: 2.1\nName: My_Pkg\nVersion: 1.0.0\n",
            )
        mock_session.get.return_value = Mock(content=buf.getvalue())

        wheel_url = "https://pkg.test/files/My_Pkg-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl"
        metadata = get_metadata_for_wheel(wheel_url)

        assert metadata.name == "My_Pkg"
        assert str(metadata.version) == "1.0.0"

    @patch("fromager.candidate.session")
    def test_get_metadata_missing_dist_info(self, mock_session: typing.Any) -> None:
        """Test that a wheel without its own dist-info raises an error."""
        buf = io.BytesIO()
        with zipfile.ZipFile(buf, "w") as zf:
            zf.writestr(
                "my_pkg/_vendor/aaa-2.0.dist-info/METADATA",
                "Metadata-Version: 2.1\nName: aaa\nVersion: 2.0\n",
            )
        mock_session.get.return_value = Mock(content=buf.getvalue())

        wheel_url = "https://pkg.test/files/my_pkg-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl"
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=r"my_pkg-1\.0\.0\.dist-info/METADATA"):
            get_metadata_for_wheel(wheel_url)

    def test_candidate_repr_with_metadata_url(self) -> None:
        """Test that Candidate representation includes metadata URL info."""
        candidate = Candidate(
            name="test-package",
            version=Version("1.0.0"),
            url="https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            has_metadata=True,
        )

        # The candidate should have the metadata URL attribute
        assert hasattr(candidate, "metadata_url")
        assert (
            candidate.metadata_url
            == "https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl.metadata"
        )

    def test_metadata_url_construction(self) -> None:
        """Test that metadata URLs are constructed correctly."""
        base_url = (
            "https://pypi.org/simple/test-package/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl"
        )
        expected_metadata_url = base_url + ".metadata"

SUPPORTED_TAGS_IGNORE_PLATFORM: frozenset[Tag] = frozenset(
    Tag(t.interpreter, t.abi, IGNORE_PLATFORM) for t in SUPPORTED_TAGS
)


@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=200)
def match_py_req(py_req: str, *, python_version: Version = PYTHON_VERSION) -> bool:
    """Python version requirement lookup with LRU cache

    Raises InvalidSpecifier on error

    SpecifierSet parsing and matching takes a non-trivial amount of time. A
    bootstrap run can spend over 10% of its time in parsing and matching
    Python version requirements.

    This function caches the result of SpecifierSet parsing and contains
    operation for Python version requirement. Most packages share similar
    constraints, e.g. ``>= 3.10``.
    """
    return python_version in SpecifierSet(py_req)


def resolve(
    *,
    ctx: context.WorkContext,
    req: Requirement,
    sdist_server_url: str,
    include_sdists: bool = True,
    include_wheels: bool = True,
    req_type: RequirementType | None = None,
    ignore_platform: bool = False,
) -> tuple[str, Version]:
    """Resolve requirement and return the best matching version.

    Returns (url, version) tuple for the highest matching version.
    """
    # Create the (reusable) resolver.
    provider = overrides.find_and_invoke(
        req.name,
        "get_resolver_provider",
        default_resolver_provider,
        ctx=ctx,
        req=req,
        include_sdists=include_sdists,
        include_wheels=include_wheels,
        sdist_server_url=sdist_server_url,
        req_type=req_type,
        ignore_platform=ignore_platform,
    )
    provider.cooldown = resolve_package_cooldown(ctx, req, req_type=req_type)
    max_age_cutoff = _compute_max_age_cutoff(ctx)
    results = find_all_matching_from_provider(
        provider, req, max_age_cutoff=max_age_cutoff
    )
    return results[0]


def default_resolver_provider(
    ctx: context.WorkContext,
    req: Requirement,
    sdist_server_url: str,
    include_sdists: bool,
    include_wheels: bool,
    req_type: RequirementType | None = None,
    ignore_platform: bool = False,
) -> (
    PyPIProvider
    | GenericProvider
    | GitHubTagProvider
    | GitLabTagProvider
    | VersionMapProvider
):
    """Lookup resolver provider to resolve package versions"""
    return PyPIProvider(
        include_sdists=include_sdists,
        include_wheels=include_wheels,
        sdist_server_url=sdist_server_url,
        constraints=ctx.constraints,
        req_type=req_type,
        ignore_platform=ignore_platform,
    )


def _has_equality_pin(req: Requirement) -> bool:
    """Return True if the requirement has a single exact ``==`` pin.

    Rejects wildcard pins (``==1.*``) and compound specifiers (``==1,>2``)
    which are not true exact version pins.
    """
    specs = list(req.specifier)
    return len(specs) == 1 and specs[0].operator == "==" and "*" not in specs[0].version


def resolve_package_cooldown(
    ctx: context.WorkContext,
    req: Requirement,
    req_type: RequirementType | None = None,
) -> Cooldown | None:
    """Compute the effective cooldown for a single package.

    Args:
        ctx: The current work context (provides the global cooldown).
        req: The package requirement being resolved.
        req_type: The requirement type (top-level, install, etc.).

    Returns:
        The cooldown to pass to the provider, or ``None`` if disabled.
    """
    if req_type == RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL and _has_equality_pin(req):
        if ctx.cooldown is not None:
            logger.info("cooldown bypassed as the top-level requirement uses == pin")
        return None

    per_package_days = ctx.package_build_info(req).resolver_min_release_age
    global_cooldown = ctx.cooldown
    if per_package_days is None:
        return global_cooldown
    if per_package_days == 0:
        return None
    # Per-package positive override: inherit bootstrap_time from global so all
    # resolutions in a single run share the same fixed cutoff point.
    bootstrap_time = (
        global_cooldown.bootstrap_time
        if global_cooldown is not None
        else datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC)
    )
    return Cooldown(
        min_age=datetime.timedelta(days=per_package_days),
        bootstrap_time=bootstrap_time,
    )

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfrq9gc7CuEZCrXsE31bv","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I fixed the bug. When a package has an entry in the constraints file, the `--max-release-age` filter is now skipped for it.\n\n**The fix** is in `find_all_matching_from_provider` in `src/fromager/resolver.py`. It checks `provider.constraints.get_constraint(req.name)` first. If there is a constraint, the age filter is skipped and an info line is logged instead:\n\n```\nboto3: skipping max release age filter because of constraint boto3==1.35.88\n```\n\n- **Multi-version mode:** a pinned old version is no longer filtered down to an empty list, so resolution now succeeds.\n- **Single-version mode:** the misleading \"keeping all to avoid empty resolution\" warning no longer appears for constrained packages.\n- **Unconstrained packages:** they are filtered exactly as before.\n\nThis exemption applies to any constraint, not only `==` pins. A range like `boto3<1.36` also turns the age filter off for that package. I chose this because the ticket says a constraint is explicit user intent. If you'd rather exempt only exact pins, it's a small change.\n\n**Regression test:** `test_max_release_age_skipped_for_constrained_package` in `tests/test_cooldown.py`. It runs with the fallback both on and off (that is, single-version and multi-version behaviour). It pins `test-pkg==1.2.2`, which is older than the age cutoff, and checks that `1.2.2` is returned and the misleading warning is not logged.\n\n**Test results:**\n- Without the source change, the new test fails in both modes: multi-version returns `[]`, and single-version logs the misleading warning.\n- With the fix, `tests/test_cooldown.py` passes (38 tests).\n- `test_resolver.py` and both `test_bootstrap_requirement_resolver*.py` files also pass.\n\nI couldn't run ruff or mypy because they aren't installed in `.venv`, so lint, formatting and type checks haven't been run. I haven't committed anything."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1328,"cache_read_input_tokens":69382,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1328},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"cbf8f10b-627d-4230-9f0b-93c9ffc25493","uuid":"2e4e7556-b061-4a7e-a411-b9a5cbbbf32d","timestamp":"2026-10-09T14:36:03.508Z","request_id":"req_011Cfrq9gKzeeAH7o28Tv4yf"}

"""Tests for the release-age cooldown policy (issue #877).

The cooldown rejects package versions published fewer than N days ago,
protecting against supply-chain attacks where a malicious version is
published and immediately pulled in by automated builds.
"""

import datetime
import logging
import pathlib
import re
import typing

import pytest
import requests_mock
import resolvelib
import yaml
from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.version import Version

from fromager import (
    candidate,
    constraints,
    context,
    packagesettings,
    resolver,
    sources,
    wheels,
)
from fromager.requirements_file import RequirementType

_BOOTSTRAP_TIME = datetime.datetime(2026, 3, 26, 0, 0, 0, tzinfo=datetime.UTC)
_COOLDOWN_7_DAYS = datetime.timedelta(days=7)
# cutoff = 2026-03-19T00:00:00Z

# Use PEP 691 JSON format — pypi_simple reliably parses upload-time from JSON.
_PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE = "application/vnd.pypi.simple.v1+json"

# Three versions at known ages:
#   2.0.0  uploaded 2026-03-24 →  2 days old (within cooldown)
#   1.3.2  uploaded 2026-03-15 → 11 days old (outside cooldown)
#   1.2.2  uploaded 2026-01-01 → 84 days old (outside cooldown)
_cooldown_json_response = {
    "meta": {"api-version": "1.1"},
    "name": "test-pkg",
    "files": [
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-2.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-2.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "aaa"},
            "upload-time": "2026-03-24T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-1.3.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-1.3.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "bbb"},
            "upload-time": "2026-03-15T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-1.2.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-1.2.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "ccc"},
            "upload-time": "2026-01-01T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
    ],
}

_all_recent_json_response = {
    "meta": {"api-version": "1.1"},
    "name": "test-pkg",
    "files": [
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-2.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-2.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "aaa"},
            "upload-time": "2026-03-25T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-1.3.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-1.3.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "bbb"},
            "upload-time": "2026-03-24T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
    ],
}

_COOLDOWN = candidate.Cooldown(
    min_age=_COOLDOWN_7_DAYS,
    bootstrap_time=_BOOTSTRAP_TIME,
)


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def clear_resolver_cache() -> typing.Generator[None, None, None]:
    """Clear the class-level resolver cache before each test.

    BaseProvider.resolver_cache is a ClassVar that persists across test
    instances. Without clearing it, candidates fetched in one test are reused
    by subsequent tests, bypassing mocked HTTP responses and producing
    incorrect results.
    """
    resolver.BaseProvider.clear_cache()
    resolver.BaseProvider._cooldown_unsupported_warned.clear()
    yield


def test_cooldown_filters_recent_version(
    caplog: pytest.LogCaptureFixture,
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    """Versions within the cooldown window are skipped; older ones are selected."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(resolver, "DEBUG_RESOLVER", "1")
    with requests_mock.Mocker() as r:
        r.get(
            "https://pypi.org/simple/test-pkg/",
            json=_cooldown_json_response,
            headers={"Content-Type": _PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE},
        )
        provider = resolver.PyPIProvider(include_sdists=True, cooldown=_COOLDOWN)
        rslvr = resolvelib.Resolver(provider, resolvelib.BaseReporter())
        with caplog.at_level(logging.DEBUG, logger="fromager.resolver"):
            result = rslvr.resolve([Requirement("test-pkg")])

        candidate = result.mapping["test-pkg"]
        # 2.0.0 is 2 days old (within cooldown); 1.3.2 is 11 days old (outside).
        assert str(candidate.version) == "1.3.2"
        # 2.0.0 should be logged as blocked; 1.3.2 should not appear in the summary.
        assert "cooldown blocked 1 version(s): 2.0.0" in caplog.text


def test_cooldown_disabled_selects_latest() -> None:
    """Without a cooldown the resolver selects the latest version as normal."""
    with requests_mock.Mocker() as r:
        r.get(
            "https://pypi.org/simple/test-pkg/",
            json=_cooldown_json_response,
            headers={"Content-Type": _PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE},
        )
        provider = resolver.PyPIProvider(include_sdists=True, cooldown=None)
        rslvr = resolvelib.Resolver(provider, resolvelib.BaseReporter())
        result = rslvr.resolve([Requirement("test-pkg")])

        candidate = result.mapping["test-pkg"]
        assert str(candidate.version) == "2.0.0"


def test_cooldown_all_blocked_raises_informative_error() -> None:
    """When all candidates are within the cooldown window the error says so."""
    with requests_mock.Mocker() as r:
        r.get(
            "https://pypi.org/simple/test-pkg/",
            json=_all_recent_json_response,
            headers={"Content-Type": _PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE},
        )
        provider = resolver.PyPIProvider(include_sdists=True, cooldown=_COOLDOWN)
        rslvr = resolvelib.Resolver(provider, resolvelib.BaseReporter())

        with pytest.raises(resolvelib.resolvers.ResolverException) as exc_info:
            rslvr.resolve([Requirement("test-pkg")])

        msg = str(exc_info.value)
        assert "2 candidate(s)" in msg
        assert "published within the last 7 days (release-age cooldown" in msg


def test_cooldown_rejects_candidate_without_upload_time(
    caplog: pytest.LogCaptureFixture,
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    """A candidate with no upload_time is rejected when a cooldown is active (fail closed)."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(resolver, "DEBUG_RESOLVER", "1")
    candidate = resolver.Candidate(
        name="test-pkg",
        version=Version("1.0.0"),
        url="https://example.com/test-pkg-1.0.0.tar.gz",
        upload_time=None,
    )
    provider = resolver.PyPIProvider(cooldown=_COOLDOWN)

    with caplog.at_level(logging.DEBUG, logger="fromager.resolver"):
        result = provider.is_blocked_by_cooldown(candidate)

    assert result is True
    assert "upload_time unknown" in caplog.text
    assert "1.0.0" in caplog.text

from __future__ import annotations

import concurrent.futures
import contextlib
import datetime
import json
import logging
import operator
import pathlib
import shutil
import tempfile
import typing

from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.utils import NormalizedName, canonicalize_name
from packaging.version import Version

from .. import (
    bootstrap_requirement_resolver,
    build_environment,
    dependencies,
    gitutils,
    progress,
    sources,
)
from ..dependency_graph import DependencyGraph
from ..log import req_ctxvar_context, requirement_ctxvar
from ..requirements_file import RequirementType, SourceType
from . import _cache
from ._build import Build
from ._phase import Phase
from ._prepare_build import PrepareBuild
from ._prepare_source import PrepareSource
from ._process_install_deps import ProcessInstallDeps
from ._resolve import Resolve
from ._types import (
    _DEFAULT_BG_THREADS,
    FailureRecord,
    FailureType,
    SeenKey,
    SourceBuildResult,
)
from ._work_item import WorkItem

if typing.TYPE_CHECKING:
    from .. import context

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class Bootstrapper:
    def __init__(
        self,
        ctx: context.WorkContext,
        progressbar: progress.Progressbar | None = None,
        prev_graph: DependencyGraph | None = None,
        cache_wheel_server_url: str | None = None,
        sdist_only: bool = False,
        test_mode: bool = False,
        multiple_versions: bool = False,
        num_bg_threads: int = _DEFAULT_BG_THREADS,
    ) -> None:
        if test_mode and sdist_only:
            raise ValueError(
                "--test-mode requires full wheel builds; incompatible with --sdist-only"
            )

        self.ctx = ctx
        self.progressbar = progressbar or progress.Progressbar(None)
        self.prev_graph = prev_graph
        self.cache_wheel_server_url = cache_wheel_server_url or ctx.wheel_server_url
        self.sdist_only = sdist_only
        self.test_mode = test_mode
        self.multiple_versions = multiple_versions
        self.why: list[tuple[RequirementType, Requirement, Version]] = []
        self._num_bg_threads = max(1, num_bg_threads)
        self._bg_pool: concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor | None = (
            concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(
                max_workers=self._num_bg_threads, thread_name_prefix="fromager-bg"
            )
        )

        # Delegate resolution to BootstrapRequirementResolver
        self._resolver = bootstrap_requirement_resolver.BootstrapRequirementResolver(
            ctx=ctx,
            prev_graph=prev_graph,
            multiple_versions=multiple_versions,
            cache_wheel_server_url=self.cache_wheel_server_url,
        )
        # Push items onto the stack as we start to resolve their
        # dependencies so at the end we have a list of items that need to
        # be built in order.
        self._build_stack: list[typing.Any] = []
        self._build_requirements: set[tuple[NormalizedName, str]] = set()

        # Track requirements we've seen before so we don't resolve the
        # same dependencies over and over and so we can break cycles in
        # the dependency list. The key is the requirements spec, rather
        # than the package, in case we do have multiple rules for the same
        # package.
        self._seen_requirements: set[SeenKey] = set()

        self._build_order_filename = self.ctx.work_dir / "build-order.json"
        self._stack_filename = self.ctx.work_dir / "bootstrap-stack.json"
        logger.info("recording bootstrap stack state to %s", self._stack_filename)

        # Track failed packages in test mode (list of typed dicts for JSON export)
        self.failed_packages: list[FailureRecord] = []

        # Track failed versions in multiple_versions mode
        self._failed_versions: dict[tuple[str, str], Exception] = {}

    @property
    def resolver(self) -> bootstrap_requirement_resolver.BootstrapRequirementResolver:
        """Public accessor for the version resolver."""
        return self._resolver

    def has_failed_version(self, pkg_name: NormalizedName, version: Version) -> bool:
        """Return True if this (pkg_name, version) has previously failed resolution."""
        return (pkg_name, str(version)) in self._failed_versions

    def _resolve_and_add_top_level(
        self,
        req: Requirement,
    ) -> tuple[str, Version] | None:
        """Resolve a top-level requirement and add it to the dependency graph.

        Private method called only by ``bootstrap()``.

        This is the pre-resolution phase before recursive bootstrapping begins.
        In test mode, catches resolution errors and records them as failures.

        When multiple_versions is enabled, resolves and adds all matching versions
        to the graph, but still returns only the first (highest) version for
        backward compatibility.

        Args:
            req: The top-level requirement to resolve.

        Returns:
            Tuple of (source_url, version) if resolution succeeded, None if it
            failed in test mode.

        Raises:
            Exception: In normal mode, re-raises any resolution error.
        """
        try:
            pbi = self.ctx.package_build_info(req)
            results = self.resolve_versions(
                req=req,
                req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,
                parent_req=None,
                return_all_versions=self.multiple_versions,
            )
            if self.multiple_versions:
                logger.info(f"resolved {len(results)} version(s) for {req}")

            # Add all resolved versions to the graph
            for source_url, version in results:
                logger.info("%s resolves to %s", req, version)
                self.ctx.dependency_graph.add_dependency(
                    parent_name=None,
                    parent_version=None,
                    req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,
                    req=req,
                    req_version=version,
                    download_url=source_url,
                    pre_built=pbi.pre_built,
                    constraint=self.ctx.constraints.get_constraint(req.name),
                )

            if not results:
                if self.multiple_versions:
                    err = RuntimeError(f"no versions found for {req}")
                    self._record_failed_version(
                        req, "unresolved", err, "no versions resolved, skipping"
                    )
                    if self.test_mode:
                        self.record_test_mode_failure(req, None, err, "resolution")
                    return None
                raise RuntimeError(f"Could not resolve any versions for {req}")

            # Return first result for backward compatibility
            return results[0]
        except Exception as err:
            if self.multiple_versions:
                self._record_failed_version(req, "unresolved", err, "failed to resolve")
                if self.test_mode:
                    self.record_test_mode_failure(req, None, err, "resolution")
                return None
            if not self.test_mode:
                raise
            self.record_test_mode_failure(req, None, err, "resolution")
            return None

    def resolve_versions(
        self,
        req: Requirement,
        req_type: RequirementType,
        parent_req: Requirement | None = None,

+    def _raise_with_dependency_chain(
+        self,
+        item: Phase,
+        err: Exception,
+    ) -> typing.NoReturn:
+        """Re-raise a phase error, naming the dependency chain that led to it.
+
+        Without the chain, the error is only attributed to whichever
+        top-level package is active in the logging context, hiding the
+        package that actually pulled in the failing requirement.
+        Top-level items have no chain and are re-raised unchanged.
+        """
+        wi = item.work_item
+        if not wi.why_snapshot:
+            raise err
+        chain = " -> ".join(
+            f"{req.name}=={version}" for _, req, version in wi.why_snapshot
+        )
+        _, parent_req, parent_version = wi.why_snapshot[-1]
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"{type(item).phase} phase failed for {wi.req}, required as "
+            f"{wi.req_type} dependency of {parent_req.name}=={parent_version} "
+            f"(dependency chain: {chain})"
+        ) from err
 
     def _record_failed_version(
         self,

{"type": "user", "message": {"role": "user", "content": "This is the fromager repository (Python wheel builder). A virtualenv with the project\nand test dependencies is already set up at `.venv`; run tests with\n`.venv/bin/python -m pytest -o addopts=\"\" tests/...`.\n\nFix the issue below. Add a regression test and run the relevant test file.\n\nIssue #1214: fromager might \"lie\" about the reason of a dependency resolution failure\n\nExpected: fromager states the exact reason of the broken dependency chain.\nActual: with ENABLE_REPEATABLE_BUILD_MODE and a broken indirect dependency, the error is\nlogged under whatever top-level package is active in the logging context, e.g.\n`ERROR its-hub: Unable to resolve requirement specifier flashinfer-python==0.6.8.post1 ...`\nwhile the real chain is its-hub -> reward-hub -> vllm and vllm is the broken arc.\nfromager should say the resolution is broken because of vllm, not its-hub."}, "timestamp": "2026-10-09T14:36:05.361Z"}

---- Iterative bootstrap: phase handlers and helpers ----\n\n    def _push_items(self, stack: list[Phase], items: list[Phase]) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Push items onto the stack and submit background tasks in LIFO order.\n\n        Submits the item that will be processed first (top of stack) to the\n        background pool first, maximising overlap between background I/O and\n        main-thread serial work.\n        \"\"\"\n        stack.extend(items)\n        if self._bg_pool is not None:\n            for item in reversed(items):\n                bg_work = item.background_work(self)\n                if bg_work is not None:\n                    item.bg_future = self._bg_pool.submit(bg_work)\n\n    def _drain_background_pool(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Drain all in-flight background tasks and recreate the pool.\n\n        Used as an exclusive-build barrier: ensures all background I/O completes\n        before an exclusive build starts. ``cancel_futures=False`` guarantees\n        every submitted task runs to completion.\n        \"\"\"\n        if self._bg_pool is not None:\n            self._bg_pool.shutdown(wait=True, cancel_futures=False)\n            self._bg_pool = concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(\n                max_workers=self._num_bg_threads, thread_name_prefix=\"fromager-bg\"\n            )\n\n    def create_unresolved_work_items(\n        self,\n        deps: typing.Iterable[Requirement],\n        dep_req_type: RequirementType,\n        parent_req: Requirement,\n        parent_version: Version,\n    ) -> list[Phase]:\n        \"\"\"Create RESOLVE-phase work items for dependencies.\n\n        Called inside a parent's _track_why context so that why_snapshot\n        captures the parent's dependency chain. Resolution and error\n        handling happen later when each item's RESOLVE phase runs.\n        \"\"\"\n        return [\n            Resolve(\n                WorkItem(\n                    req=dep,\n                    req_type=dep_req_type,\n                    why_snapshot=list(self.why),\n                    parent=(parent_req, parent_version),\n                )\n            )\n            for dep in self._sort_requirements(deps)\n        ]\n\n    def _resolve_build_system_versions_by_name(\n        self,\n        build_system_deps: set[Requirement],\n    ) -> dict[NormalizedName, tuple[Version, str]]:\n        \"\"\"Build a mapping of resolved build-system versions by looking up graph nodes.\n\n        Used by the git URL path where the parent node may not yet exist\n        in the dependency graph.\n        \"\"\"\n        resolved: dict[NormalizedName, tuple[Version, str]] = {}\n        for dep in build_system_deps:\n            dep_name = canonicalize_name(dep.name)\n            nodes = self.ctx.dependency_graph.get_nodes_by_name(str(dep_name))\n            for node in nodes:\n                if node.version in dep.specifier:\n                    resolved[dep_name] = (node.version, node.download_url)\n                    break\n        return resolved\n\n    def get_resolved_build_system_versions(\n        self,\n        item: WorkItem,\n    ) -> dict[NormalizedName, tuple[Version, str]]:\n        \"\"\"Build a mapping of resolved build-system dependency versions.\n\n        Looks up the parent node's ``BUILD_SYSTEM`` edges in the dependency\n        graph to find what versions were resolved for each build-system\n        dependency.\n\n        Returns:\n            Mapping of canonicalized package name to ``(version, download_url)``.\n        \"\"\"\n        assert item.resolved_version is not None\n        parent_key = f\"{canonicalize_name(item.req.name)}=={item.resolved_version}\"\n        parent_node = self.ctx.dependency_graph.nodes.get(parent_key)\n        if parent_node is None:\n            return {}\n        resolved: dict[NormalizedName, tuple[Version, str]] = {}\n        for edge in parent_node.children:\n            if edge.req_type == RequirementType.BUILD_SYSTEM:\n                child = edge.destination_node\n                resolved[child.canonicalized_name] = (\n                    child.version,\n                    child.download_url,\n                )\n        return resolved\n\n    def filter_deps_satisfied_by_build_system(\n        self,\n        deps: set[Requirement],\n        resolved_build_sys: dict[NormalizedName, tuple[Version, str]],\n        dep_req_type: RequirementType,\n        parent: tuple[Requirement, Version] | None = None,\n    ) -> set[Requirement]:\n        \"\"\"Filter out deps already satisfied by build-system dependencies.\n\n        For each dep whose resolved build-system version satisfies the\n        requirement specifier, excludes the dep from the returned set.\n        When *parent* is provided, also adds a graph edge reusing that\n        version.  Remaining deps need independent resolution.\n\n        Logs a warning when the same package appears in both build-system\n        and build-backend/sdist with incompatible version specifiers.\n        \"\"\"\n        unsatisfied: set[Requirement] = set()\n        for dep in deps:\n            if dep.extras:\n                unsatisfied.add(dep)\n                continue\n            dep_name = canonicalize_name(dep.name)\n            if dep_name in resolved_build_sys:\n                version, download_url = resolved_build_sys[dep_name]\n                if version in dep.specifier:\n                    logger.info(\n                        \"%s dependency %s is already satisfied by \"\n                        \"build-system dependency %s==%s\",\n                        dep_req_type,\n                        dep,\n                        dep_name,\n                        version,\n                    )\n                    if parent is not None:\n                        self.add_to_graph(\n                            req=dep,\n                            req_type=dep_req_type,\n                            req_version=version,\n                            download_url=download_url,\n                            parent=parent,\n                        )\n                    continue\n                else:\n                    logger.warning(\n                        \"%s dependency %s conflicts with \"\n                        \"build-system dependency %s==%s; \"\n                        \"resolving independently\",\n                        dep_req_type,\n                        dep,\n                        dep_name,\n                        version,\n                    )\n            unsatisfied.add(dep)\n        return unsatisfied\n\n    def _handle_phase_error(\n        self,\n        item: Phase,\n        err: Exception,\n    ) -> list[Phase]:\n        \"\"\"Handle errors from phase processing.\n\n        Returns work items to continue processing (e.g. prebuilt fallback),\n        or empty list to skip this item. Raises in normal mode (fail-fast).\n        \"\"\"\n        wi = item.work_item\n        # Resolution failures: recoverable in test mode and multiple versions mode\n        if isinstance(item, Resolve):\n            if self.test_mode:\n                self.record_test_mode_failure(wi.req, None, err, \"resolution\")\n                if self.multiple_versions:\n                    self._record_failed_version(\n                        wi.req,\n                        \"unresolved\",\n                        err,\n                        f\"failed during {type(item).phase} phase\",\n                    )\n                return []\n            if self.multiple_versions:\n                self._record_failed_version(\n                    wi.req,\n                    \"unresolved\",\n                    err,\n                    f\"failed during {type(item).phase} phase\",\n                )\n                return []\n            raise\n\n        # req_type=build_type)\n                self.why = saved_why\n            self.progressbar.update()\n\n    def _download_prebuilt(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        req_type: RequirementType,\n        resolved_version: Version,\n        wheel_url: str,\n    ) -> tuple[pathlib.Path, pathlib.Path]:\n        result = _cache._bg_prepare_prebuilt(\n            self.ctx, req, req_type, resolved_version, wheel_url\n        )\n        assert result.wheel_filename is not None\n        assert result.unpack_dir is not None\n        return (result.wheel_filename, result.unpack_dir)\n\n    def _download_source(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        resolved_version: Version,\n        source_url: str,\n    ) -> pathlib.Path:\n        \"\"\"Download source for a package.\"\"\"\n        result: pathlib.Path = sources.download_source(\n            ctx=self.ctx,\n            req=req,\n            version=resolved_version,\n            download_url=source_url,\n        )\n        return result\n\n    def _prepare_source(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        resolved_version: Version,\n        source_filename: pathlib.Path,\n    ) -> pathlib.Path:\n        \"\"\"Prepare (unpack/patch) source for building.\"\"\"\n        result: pathlib.Path = sources.prepare_source(\n            ctx=self.ctx,\n            req=req,\n            source_filename=source_filename,\n            version=resolved_version,\n        )\n        return result\n\n    def _handle_test_mode_failure(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        resolved_version: Version,\n        req_type: RequirementType,\n        build_error: Exception,\n    ) -> SourceBuildResult | None:\n        \"\"\"Handle build failure in test mode by attempting pre-built fallback.\n\n        Args:\n            req: The requirement that failed to build.\n            resolved_version: The version that was attempted.\n            req_type: The type of requirement (for fallback resolution).\n            build_error: The original exception from the build attempt.\n\n        Returns:\n            SourceBuildResult if fallback succeeded, None if fallback also failed.\n        \"\"\"\n        logger.warning(\n            \"test mode: build failed for %s==%s, attempting pre-built fallback: %s\",\n            req.name,\n            resolved_version,\n            build_error,\n        )\n\n        try:\n            parent_req = self.why[-1][1] if self.why else None\n            results = self._resolver.resolve(\n                req=req,\n                req_type=req_type,\n                parent_req=parent_req,\n                pre_built=True,  # Force prebuilt for test mode fallback\n            )\n            wheel_url, fallback_version = results[0]\n\n            if fallback_version != resolved_version:\n                logger.warning(\n                    \"test mode: version mismatch for %s - requested %s, fallback %s\",\n                    req.name,\n                    resolved_version,\n                    fallback_version,\n                )\n\n            wheel_filename, unpack_dir = self._download_prebuilt(\n                req=req,\n                req_type=req_type,\n                resolved_version=fallback_version,\n                wheel_url=wheel_url,\n            )\n\n            logger.info(\n                \"test mode: successfully used pre-built wheel for %s==%s\",\n                req.name,\n                fallback_version,\n            )\n\n            # Package succeeded via fallback - no failure to record\n\n            return SourceBuildResult(\n                wheel_filename=wheel_filename,\n                sdist_filename=None,\n                unpack_dir=unpack_dir,\n                sdist_root_dir=None,\n                build_env=None,\n                source_type=SourceType.PREBUILT,\n            )\n\n        except Exception as fallback_error:\n            logger.error(\n                \"test mode: pre-built fallback also failed for %s: %s\",\n                req.name,\n                fallback_error,\n                exc_info=True,\n            )\n            # Return None to signal failure; bootstrap() will record via re-raised exception\n            return None\n\n    def _resolve_version_from_git_url(self, req: Requirement) -> tuple[str, Version]:\n        \"\"\"Resolve source path and version from a ``git+`` URL.\n\n        Parses the URL for an ``@ref`` version hint. If the ref is a valid\n        version, reuses an existing clone when possible. Otherwise, clones\n        the repo and extracts the version from package metadata.\n        \"\"\"\n\n        if not req.url:\n            raise ValueError(f\"unable to resolve from URL with no URL in {req}\")\n\n        # We start by not knowing where we would put the source because we don't\n        # know the version.\n        working_src_dir: pathlib.Path | None = None\n        version: Version | None = None\n\n        url_to_clone, git_ref = gitutils.parse_vcs_url(req.url, require_ref=False)\n        need_to_clone = False\n\n        if git_ref == gitutils.GIT_HEAD:\n            # No ref in URL, clone to discover the version.\n            logger.debug(\"no reference in URL, will clone\")\n            need_to_clone = True\n        else:\n            # If we have a reference, it might be a valid python version\n            # string, or not. It _must_ be a valid git reference. If it can\n            # be parsed as a valid python version, we assume the tag points\n            # to source that will think that is its version, so we allow\n            # reusing an existing cloned repo if there is one.\n            try:\n                version = Version(git_ref)\n            except ValueError:\n                logger.info(\n                    \"could not parse %r as a version, cloning to get the version\",\n                    git_ref,\n                )\n                need_to_clone = True\n            else:\n                logger.info(\"URL %s includes version %s\", req.url, version)\n                working_src_dir = (\n                    self.ctx.work_dir\n                    / f\"{req.name}-{version}\"\n                    / f\"{req.name}-{version}\"\n                )\n                if not working_src_dir.exists():\n                    need_to_clone = True\n                else:\n                    if self.ctx.cleanup:\n                        logger.debug(\"cleaning up %s to reclone\", working_src_dir)\n                        shutil.rmtree(working_src_dir)\n                        need_to_clone = True\n                    else:\n                        logger.info(\"reusing %s\", working_src_dir)\n\n        if need_to_clone:\n            with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:\n                clone_dir = pathlib.Path(tmpdir) / \"src\"\n                sources.download_git_source(\n                    ctx=self.ctx,\n                    req=req,\n                    url_to_clone=url_to_clone,\n                    destination_dir=clone_dir,\n                    ref=git_ref,\n                )\n                if not version:\n                    # If we still do not have a version, get it from the package\n                    # metadata.\n                    version = self._get_version_from_package_metadata(req, clone_dir)\n                    logger.info(\"found version %s\", version)\n                    working_src_dir = (\n                        self.ctx.work_dir\n                        / f\"{req.name}-{version}\"\n                        / f\"{req.name}-{version}\"\n                    )\n                    if working_src_dir.exists():\n                        # We have to check if the destination directory exists\n                        # because if we were not given a version we did not\n                        # clean it up earlier. We do not use ctx.cleanup to\n                        # control this action because we cannot trust that the\n                        # destination directory is reusable because we have had\n                        # to compute the version and we cannot be sure that the\n                        # version is dynamic. Two different commits in the repo\n                        # could have the same version if that version is set\n                        # with static data in the repo instead of via a tag or\n                        # dynamically computed by something like setuptools-scm.\n                        logger.debug(\"cleaning up %s\", working_src_dir)\n                        shutil.rmtree(working_src_dir)\n                assert working_src_dir is not None\n                working_src_dir.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n                logger.info(\"moving cloned repo to %s\", working_src_dir)\n                shutil.move(clone_dir, str(working_src_dir))\n\n        if not version:\n            raise ValueError(f\"unable to determine version for {req}\")\n\n        if not working_src_dir:\n            raise ValueError(f\"unable to determine working source directory for {req}\")\n\n        logging.info(\"resolved from git URL to %s, %s\", working_src_dir, version)\n        return (str(working_src_dir), version)\n\n    def _get_version_from_package_metadata(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        source_dir: pathlib.Path,\n    ) -> Version:\n        pbi = self.ctx.package_build_info(req)\n        build_dir = pbi.build_dir(source_dir)\n\n        logger.info(\n            \"preparing build dependencies so we can access the metadata to get the version\"\n        )\n        build_env = build_environment.BuildEnvironment(\n            ctx=self.ctx,\n            parent_dir=source_dir.parent,\n        )\n        build_dependencies = self._prepare_build_dependencies(\n            req=req,\n            resolved_version=None,\n            sdist_root_dir=source_dir,\n            build_env=build_env,\n        )\n        build_env.install(build_dependencies)\n\n        logger.info(\"generating metadata to get version\")\n        hook_caller = dependencies.get_build_backend_hook_caller(\n            ctx=self.ctx,\n            req=req,\n            build_dir=build_dir,\n            override_environ={},\n            build_env=build_env,\n        )\n        metadata_dir_base = hook_caller.prepare_metadata_for_build_wheel(\n            metadata_directory=str(source_dir.parent),\n            config_settings=pbi.config_settings,\n        )\n        metadata_filename = source_dir.parent / metadata_dir_base / \"METADATA\"\n        # Disable validation because some packages have metadata version mismatches\n        # (e.g., declaring Metadata-Version: 2.2 but using fields from 2.4).\n        metadata = dependencies.parse_metadata(metadata_filename, validate=False)\n        return metadata.version\n\n    def add_to_graph(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        req_type: RequirementType,\n        req_version: Version,\n        download_url: str,\n        parent: tuple[Requirement, Version] | None,\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Add a resolved requirement as a node/edge in the dependency graph.\n\n        Records the dependency relationship between ``parent`` and ``req`` in\n        the in-memory graph, then writes the updated graph to disk. Must be\n        called after resolution but before the seen-check so that every edge\n        is captured even for packages that are not built again.\n\n        Args:\n            req: The requirement being added.\n            req_type: Whether this is a build-system, build-backend, install,\n                or other dependency kind.\n            req_version: The resolved version of ``req``.\n            download_url: Source URL used to obtain the distribution.\n            parent: ``(req, version)`` of the package that introduced ``req``,\n                or ``None`` for top-level requirements.\n        \"\"\"\n        parent_req, parent_version = parent if parent else (None, None)\n        pbi = self.ctx.package_build_info(req)\n        # Update the dependency graph after we determine that this requirement is\n        # useful but before we determine if it is redundant so that we capture all\n        # edges to use for building a valid constraints file.\n        self.ctx.dependency_graph.add_dependency(\n            parent_name=canonicalize_name(parent_req.name) if parent_req else None,\n            parent_version=parent_version,\n            req_type=req_type,\n            req=req,\n            req_version=req_version,\n            download_url=download_url,\n            pre_built=pbi.pre_built,\n            constraint=self.ctx.constraints.get_constraint(req.name),\n        )\n        self.ctx.write_to_graph_to_file()\n\n    def _sort_requirements(\n        self,\n        requirements: typing.Iterable[Requirement],\n    ) -> typing.Iterable[Requirement]:\n        return sorted(requirements, key=operator.attrgetter(\"name\"))\n\n    def _resolved_key(\n        self, req: Requirement, version: Version, typ: typing.Literal[\"sdist\", \"wheel\"]\n    ) -> SeenKey:\n        return (\n            canonicalize_name(req.name),\n            tuple(sorted(req.extras)),\n            str(version),\n            typ,\n        )\n\n    def mark_as_seen(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        version: Version,\n        sdist_only: bool = False,\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Track sdist and wheel builds\n\n        A sdist-only build just contains as an sdist.\n        A wheel build counts as wheel and sdist, because the presence of a\n        either implies we have built a wheel from an sdist or we have a\n        prebuilt wheel that will never have an sdist.\n        \"\"\"\n        # Mark sdist seen for sdist-only build and wheel build\n        self._seen_requirements.add(self._resolved_key(req, version, \"sdist\"))\n        if not sdist_only:\n            # Mark wheel seen only for wheel build\n            self._seen_requirements.add(self._resolved_key(req, version, \"wheel\"))\n\n    def has_been_seen(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        version: Version,\n        sdist_only: bool = False,\n    ) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"Return True if this requirement/version has already been processed.\n\n        Uses the same sdist-vs-wheel distinction as ``mark_as_seen``:\n        when ``sdist_only`` is True, checks only for a prior sdist build;\n        otherwise checks for a prior wheel build.\n\n        Args:\n            req: The requirement to check.\n            version: The resolved version to check.\n            sdist_only: If True, check for a sdist-only build instead of a\n                full wheel build.\n        \"\"\"\n        typ: typing.Literal[\"sdist\", \"wheel\"] = \"sdist\" if sdist_only else \"wheel\"\n        return self._resolved_key(req, version, typ) in self._seen_requirements\n\n    def add_to_build_order(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        version: Version,\n        source_url: str,\n        source_type: SourceType,\n        prebuilt: bool = False,\n        constraint: Requirement | None = None,\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Append a package to the build-order output file if not already present.\n\n        Deduplicates by ``(canonicalized_name, version)`` so the same package\n        is never written twice, regardless of extras. On each new entry, the\n        full build-order list is written to ``self._build_order_filename``.\n\n        Args:\n            req: The requirement being added to the build order.\n            version: The resolved version.\n            source_url: URL from which the source distribution was obtained.\n            source_type: The kind of source (sdist, wheel, git, etc.).\n            prebuilt: True if the wheel was taken from a prebuilt cache rather\n                than compiled locally.\n            constraint: The version constraint active for this package, if any.\n        \"\"\"\n        # We only care if this version of this package has been built,\n        # and don't want to trigger building it twice. The \"extras\"\n        # value, included in the _resolved_key() output, can confuse\n        # that so we ignore itand build our own key using just the\n        # name and version.\n        key = (canonicalize_name(req.name), str(version))\n        if key in self._build_requirements:\n            return\n        logger.info(f\"adding {key} to build order\")\n        self._build_requirements.add(key)\n        info = {\n            \"req\": str(req),\n            \"constraint\": str(constraint) if constraint else \"\",\n            \"dist\": canonicalize_name(req.name),\n            \"version\": str(version),\n            \"prebuilt\": prebuilt,\n            \"source_url\": source_url,\n            \"source_url_type\": str(source_type),\n        }\n        if req.url:\n            info[\"source_url\"] = req.url\n        self._build_stack.append(info)\n        with open(self._build_order_filename, \"w\") as f:\n            # Set default=str because the why value includes\n            # Requirement and Version instances that can't be\n            # converted to JSON without help.\n            json.dump(self._build_stack, f, indent=2, default=str)\n\n    def _record_stack_state(self, stack: list[Phase]) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Write the current bootstrap stack to `self._stack_filename`.\n\n        Index 0 in the output corresponds to `stack[-1]`, the next item to be\n        processed. Overwrites the file on each call.\n        \"\"\"\n        records = [item.as_json() for item in reversed(stack)]\n        with open(self._stack_filename, \"w\") as f:\n            json.dump(records, f, indent=2, default=str)\n\n    # ---- Iterative bootstrap: phase handlers and helpers ----\n\n    def _push_items(self, stack: list[Phase], items: list[Phase]) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Push items onto the stack and submit background tasks in LIFO order.\n\n        Submits the item that will be processed first (top of stack) to the\n        background pool first, maximising overlap between background I/O and\n        main-thread serial work.\n        \"\"\"\n        stack.extend(items)\n        if self._bg_pool is not None:\n            for item in reversed(items):\n                bg_work = item.background_work(self)\n                if bg_work is not None:\n                    item.bg_future = self._bg_pool.submit(bg_work)\n\n    def _drain_background_pool(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Drain all in-flight background tasks and recreate the pool.\n\n        Used as an exclusive-build barrier: ensures all background I/O completes\n        before an exclusive build starts. ``cancel_futures=False`` guarantees\n        every submitted task runs to completion.\n        \"\"\"\n        if self._bg_pool is not None:\n            self._bg_pool.shutdown(wait=True, cancel_futures=False)\n            self._bg_pool = concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(\n                max_workers=self._num_bg_threads, thread_name_prefix=\"fromager-bg\"\n            )\n\n    def create_unresolved_work_items(\n        self,\n        deps: typing.Iterable[Requirement],\n        dep_req_type: RequirementType,\n        parent_req: Requirement,\n        parent_version: Version,\n    ) -> list[Phase]:\n        \"\"\"Create RESOLVE-phase work items for dependencies.\n\n        Called inside a parent's _track_why context so that why_snapshot\n        captures the parent's dependency chain. Resolution and error\n        handling happen later when each item's RESOLVE phase runs.\n        \"\"\"\n        return [\n            Resolve(\n                WorkItem(\n                    req=dep,\n                    req_type=dep_req_type,\n                    why_snapshot=list(self.why),\n                    parent=(parent_req, parent_version),\n                )\n            )\n            for dep in self._sort_requirements(deps)\n        ]\n\n    def _resolve_build_system_versions_by_name(\n        self,\n        build_system_deps: set[Requirement],\n    ) -> dict[NormalizedName, tuple[Version, str]]:\n        \"\"\"Build a mapping of resolved build-system versions by looking up graph nodes.\n\n        Used by the git URL path where the parent node may not yet exist\n        in the dependency graph.\n        \"\"\"\n        resolved: dict[NormalizedName, tuple[Version, str]] = {}\n        for dep in build_system_deps:\n            dep_name = canonicalize_name(dep.name)\n            nodes = self.ctx.dependency_graph.get_nodes_by_name(str(dep_name))\n            for node in nodes:\n                if node.version in dep.specifier:\n                    resolved[dep_name] = (node.version, node.download_url)\n                    break\n        return resolved\n\n    def get_resolved_build_system_versions(\n        self,\n        item: WorkItem,\n    ) -> dict[NormalizedName, tuple[Version, str]]:\n        \"\"\"Build a mapping of resolved build-system dependency versions.\n\n        Looks up the parent node's ``BUILD_SYSTEM`` edges in the dependency\n        graph to find what versions were resolved for each build-system\n        dependency.\n\n        Returns:\n            Mapping of canonicalized package name to ``(version, download_url)``.\n        \"\"\"\n        assert item.resolved_version is not None\n        parent_key = f\"{canonicalize_name(item.req.name)}=={item.resolved_version}\"\n        parent_node = self.ctx.dependency_graph.nodes.get(parent_key)\n        if parent_node is None:\n            return {}\n        resolved: dict[NormalizedName, tuple[Version, str]] = {}\n        for edge in parent_node.children:\n            if edge.req_type == RequirementType.BUILD_SYSTEM:\n                child = edge.destination_node\n                resolved[child.canonicalized_name] = (\n                    child.version,\n                    child.download_url,\n                )\n        return resolved\n\n    def filter_deps_satisfied_by_build_system(\n        self,\n        deps: set[Requirement],\n        resolved_build_sys: dict[NormalizedName, tuple[Version, str]],\n        dep_req_type: RequirementType,\n        parent: tuple[Requirement, Version] | None = None,\n    ) -> set[Requirement]:\n        \"\"\"Filter out deps already satisfied by build-system dependencies.\n\n        For each dep whose resolved build-system version satisfies the\n        requirement specifier, excludes the dep from the returned set.\n        When *parent* is provided, also adds a graph edge reusing that\n        version.  Remaining deps need independent resolution.\n\n        Logs a warning when the same package appears in both build-system\n        and build-backend/sdist with incompatible version specifiers.\n        \"\"\"\n        unsatisfied: set[Requirement] = set()\n        for dep in deps:\n            if dep.extras:\n                unsatisfied.add(dep)\n                continue\n            dep_name = canonicalize_name(dep.name)\n            if dep_name in resolved_build_sys:\n                version, download_url = resolved_build_sys[dep_name]\n                if version in dep.specifier:\n                    logger.info(\n                        \"%s dependency %s is already satisfied by \"\n                        \"build-system dependency %s==%s\",\n                        dep_req_type,\n                        dep,\n                        dep_name,\n                        version,\n                    )\n                    if parent is not None:\n                        self.add_to_graph(\n                            req=dep,\n                            req_type=dep_req_type,\n                            req_version=version,\n                            download_url=download_url,\n                            parent=parent,\n                        )\n                    continue\n                else:\n                    logger.warning(\n                        \"%s dependency %s conflicts with \"\n                        \"build-system dependency %s==%s; \"\n                        \"resolving independently\",\n                        dep_req_type,\n                        dep,\n                        dep_name,\n                        version,\n                    )\n            unsatisfied.add(dep)\n        return unsatisfied\n\n    def _handle_phase_error(\n        self,\n        item: Phase,\n        err: Exception,\n    ) -> list[Phase]:\n        \"\"\"Handle errors from phase processing.\n\n        Returns work items to continue processing (e.g. prebuilt fallback),\n        or empty list to skip this item. Raises in normal mode (fail-fast).\n        \"\"\"\n        wi = item.work_item\n        # Resolution failures: recoverable in test mode and multiple versions mode\n        if isinstance(item, Resolve):\n            if self.test_mode:\n                self.record_test_mode_failure(wi.req, None, err, \"resolution\")\n                if self.multiple_versions:\n                    self._record_failed_version(\n                        wi.req,\n                        \"unresolved\",\n                        err,\n                        f\"failed during {type(item).phase} phase\",\n                    )\n                return []\n            if self.multiple_versions:\n                self._record_failed_version(\n                    wi.req,\n                    \"unresolved\",\n                    err,\n                    f\"failed during {type(item).phase} phase\",\n                )\n                return []\n            raise\n\n        # Test mode: try prebuilt fallback for build-related phases\n        if self.test_mode:\n            if (\n                isinstance(item, PrepareSource | PrepareBuild | Build)\n                and not wi.pbi_pre_built\n            ):\n                assert wi.resolved_version is not None\n                fallback = self._handle_test_mode_failure(\n                    req=wi.req,\n                    resolved_version=wi.resolved_version,\n                    req_type=wi.req_type,\n                    build_error=err,\n                )\n                if fallback is not None:\n                    wi.build_result = fallback\n                    return [ProcessInstallDeps(wi)]\n            self.record_test_mode_failure(\n                wi.req, str(wi.resolved_version), err, \"bootstrap\"\n            )\n            return []\n\n        # Multiple versions mode: record failure, remove from graph, continue\n        if self.multiple_versions:\n            assert wi.resolved_version is not None\n            pkg_name = canonicalize_name(wi.req.name)\n            self._record_failed_version(\n                wi.req,\n                str(wi.resolved_version),\n                err,\n                f\"failed during {type(item).phase} phase\",\n            )\n            self.ctx.dependency_graph.remove_dependency(pkg_name, wi.resolved_version)\n            self._seen_requirements.discard(\n                self._resolved_key(wi.req, wi.resolved_version, \"sdist\")\n            )\n            self._seen_requirements.discard(\n                self._resolved_key(wi.req, wi.resolved_version, \"wheel\")\n            )\n            self.ctx.write_to_graph_to_file()\n            return []\n\n        # Normal mode: fail-fast\n        raise\n\n    def _record_failed_version(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        version: str,\n        err: Exception,\n        detail: str,\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Record a version failure in multiple versions mode.\"\"\"\n        pkg_name = canonicalize_name(req.name)\n        self._failed_versions[(pkg_name, version)] = err\n        logger.warning(\n            \"%s==%s: %s: %s: %s\",\n            req.name,\n            version,\n            detail,\n            type(err).__name__,\n            err,\n        )\n\n    def _log_failed_versions_table(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Log a summary table of all failed versions.\"\"\"\n        logger.warning(\"%d version(s) failed to bootstrap:\", len(self._failed_versions))\n        for (name, ver), exc in self._failed_versions.items():\n            logger.warning(\"  %s==%s: %s: %s\", name, ver, type(exc).__name__, exc)\n\n    def finalize(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Finalize bootstrap and return exit code.\n\n        Reports failed versions in multiple versions mode.\n        In test mode, writes failure report and returns non-zero if there were failures.\n\n        Returns:\n            0 if all packages built successfully (or not in test/multiple versions mode)\n            1 if any packages failed in test mode\n        \"\"\"\n        if self._bg_pool is not None:\n            # cancel_futures=True cancels pending (not-yet-started) futures immediately\n            # so we don't block waiting for work whose result will never be used.\n            # Already-running futures still complete naturally.\n            self._bg_pool.shutdown(wait=True, cancel_futures=True)\n            self._bg_pool = None\n\n        if self.multiple_versions and self._failed_versions:\n            self._log_failed_versions_table()\n\n        if not self.test_mode:\n            return 0\n\n        if not self.failed_packages:\n            logger.info(\"test mode: all packages processed successfully\")\n            return 0\n\n        # Write JSON failure report with timestamp for uniqueness\n        timestamp = datetime.datetime.now(tz=datetime.UTC).strftime(\"%Y%m%d-%H%M%S-%f\")\n        failures_file = self.ctx.work_dir / f\"test-mode-failures-{timestamp}.json\"\n        with open(failures_file, \"w\") as f:\n            json.dump({\"failures\": self.failed_packages}, f, indent=2)\n        logger.info(\"test mode: wrote failure report to %s\", failures_file)\n\n        #
